chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Setting the record straight on Shelly Manne and a 'floating rhythm section'
summary: He denies a floating rhythm section with Manne and Heywood; Manne, then in the Navy, learned by sitting in.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I think I mentioned to you, it was last year, that Shelly Mann said that you and he and Eddie Heywood used to have a floating rhythm section and go around to sessions in New York. Where ever there was going to be a session, you'd go in and be the rhythm section and you said that wasn't true?

Shelly Mann was in the Navy. He was stationed at Sheepshead Bay with Dick Stabile. Now he learned how to play drums but he didn't know anything about jazz. And Kenny Clark who they called Klook, just suffered a stroke recently in Paris which that broke up the Clarke Bold Band. I would ask -- Shelly would ask me "Can I sit in, can I sit in." And stayed on this so long, I'd say let the man sit in. All right he'd come on. But when he was real tired, or he wanted to talk to a girl or you know something, so Shelly would get on the stand and I'd have to tell him how to cock his cymbals to get the sound that Jo Jones got and what cymbal to play behind when he played, you know. And Nat Jaffe was playing piano.

And oh, he was so far ahead of his time as far as (chorus) structure. Oh! He was playing then what they're playing now. In 1941. And he had a heart attack and he was living at 107th and Central Park. I use to go by and visit him quite a bit. Yeah, good a -- old days.
So when Shelly got out of the Navy, did he show up again?
No, his wife was one of the Rockettes. Not the Rockettes, Radio City.
Yeah, yeah. And they moved out here. Well he had enough to go on and came out here and got into the
It was on 52nd street, when he use to come in and ask to jam?
He never played with Eddie Heywood when you played with Eddie Heywood?
